chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered an aged old man who had never performed Hajj and could not endure Hajj due to his old age to prepare a man to perform Hajj on his behalf.

key_terms.يَحُجَّ عَنْهُ: To perform Hajj on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly person who cannot physically perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of Hajj al-Badal, specifying that the obligation is fulfilled by equipping a capable substitute rather than merely sending money. It highlights the scholarly consensus in Shia jurisprudence that physical incapacity, such as advanced age, permits this delegation, ensuring the spiritual duty is met without undue hardship. The emphasis on 'equipping' (ijhaz) underscores the necessity of covering the substitute's expenses and logistical needs for the ritual to be valid.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> ordered an aged old man who had not performed Hajj at all and could not endure the Hajj due to his age that he should prepare a man who would perform Hajj on his behalf’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, Alayhi al-Salam, commanded an old man who had never performed al-Hajj and was not able to perform al-Hajj because of old age to prepare a man to perform al-Hajj on his behalf.’”
